pages.title: Competition
pages.content:
Neural Interfaces 2026 · Track 02 · Cross-session shift

BCI decoding

Decodes a cued mental command — motor imagery, mental calculation, word association — from short EEG windows.

The controlled shift is cross-session: models train on early sessions and are scored on later sessions of the same subject, with no per-session recalibration allowed.

Ranking metric
Balanced accuracy (plain accuracy reported alongside)
Controlled shift
Cross-session — no recalibration
Signals & context
Motor imagery, mental math, word association, session drift
Track sponsor
Meta FAIR Brain & AI

The task

Epoched classification: one label per window. Your model receives torch batches X: (B, C, T) and must return one predicted class per window, predict(X) -> (B,). Scoring is balanced accuracy over the held-out split, so every class counts equally regardless of its frequency.

The data comes through the neuralbench eeg/motor_imagery task config (4-s stimulus windows, subject-level split). The starting kit exposes three study overlays: stieger2021 (Stieger2021Continuous — the public proxy, 62 subjects, 4-class, large download), tangermann2012 (BNCI2014_001 — small, handy for real-data smoke tests) and dreyer2023 (Dreyer2023Large — official-candidate dataset, 2-class, predefined train/test subjects). A zero-dependency Simulated dataset ships for no-network smoke tests.

Leaderboard columns

ColumnKeySorting
Balanced accuracybalanced_accuracyhigher is better — ranking metric
Accuracyaccuracyhigher is better
Duration (s)durationlower is better

See the Participation tab for the submission contract and the starting kit, and the Timeline tab for phase dates.

One benchmark. Four real shifts.

Biosignal foundation models claim to transfer across subjects, sessions and devices with limited per-task training. This challenge tests that claim against strong task-specific baselines.

The four-track design separates two claims usually conflated in the literature: single-task performance and shift robustness. One harness and one reproducibility audit hold evaluation fixed, so a per-track score can be attributed to the model rather than the protocol.

The track described above is this competition. The other three run as their own Codabench competitions, each with its own leaderboard, under the same harness, the same rules and the same audit — one team may enter all four.

pages.title: Participation
pages.content:
# How to participate

Your submission is a folder containing a `submission.py` that defines a
**benchopt solver**, plus any weight files your model needs. The competition
server evaluates it **inference-only**: your model must arrive fully trained.

## The contract

Subclass `CompetSolver` (from the bundled `compet_core` package) and
implement:

- `load_model(self, meta)` — build your model and load your shipped weights
  from `meta["weights_dir"]`, placing it on `meta["device"]`. Return an
  object exposing `predict(X)`.
- `predict(X)` receives torch batches `X: (B, C, T)` already on
  `meta["device"]`; the expected output shape is track-specific (see the
  competition description — e.g. class labels `(B,)`, latencies `(B,)`,
  embeddings `(B, D)`, or joint-angle sequences `(B, J, T)`).

`meta` also carries `sfreq, ch_names, chs_info, n_chans, n_times` and the
track's output size (`n_classes` / `n_outputs` / `n_joints`).

Optionally, implement `fit(self, model, train_loader)` — it only runs
**locally** (never on the server) and lets you train your model with the
exact competition data through the starting kit.

```python
import torch

import benchmark_utils  # noqa: F401 — locates compet_core
from compet_core.base_solver import CompetSolver


class Solver(CompetSolver):
    name = "MyModel"
    requirements = CompetSolver.requirements + ["pip::my-model-pkg"]

    def load_model(self, meta):
        model = build_my_model(
            n_chans=meta["n_chans"], n_times=meta["n_times"],
        )
        state = torch.load(meta["weights_dir"] / "weights.pt",
                           map_location=meta["device"])
        model.load_state_dict(state)
        return model.to(meta["device"]).eval()
```

Your `predict` can be a method of the returned model (plain PyTorch — no
benchopt, neuralset or neuralbench knowledge is needed inside your model).

## Test locally

The starting kit is the benchmark itself. From the competition repo (no
install of the repo needed — `benchmark_utils` locates the shared
`compet_core` package):

```bash
benchopt install tracks/<track>    # solvers/datasets requirements
benchopt run tracks/<track> -d Simulated   # zero-download smoke test
```

To iterate on a submission before uploading, drop your `submission.py` into
the track's `solvers/` folder and run the same command; or mirror the
platform exactly with the ingestion program:

```bash
python codabench/ingestion_program/ingestion.py \
    --submission-dir my_submission/ \
    --benchmark-dir tracks/<track> --datasets Simulated
python codabench/scoring_program/scoring.py \
    --prediction-dir output/ --output-dir scores/
```

Training on the real data locally: `python tools/setup_data.py --track
<track>` downloads it once, then use your solver's `fit` with
`benchopt run tracks/<track>`.

## Submit

Zip the submission folder (`submission.py` + weights) and upload it on the
*My Submissions* tab. Baselines and reference submissions live in the
`solution/` folder of the bundle.
pages.content_zh:
# 如何参与

您的提交是一个包含 `submission.py` 的文件夹，该文件定义一个 **benchopt 求解器**，以及您的模型所需的任何权重文件。竞赛服务器仅对其进行**推理评估**：您的模型必须已完全训练好。

## 协议

继承 `CompetSolver`（来自捆绑的 `compet_core` 包）并实现：

- `load_model(self, meta)` — 构建您的模型并从 `meta["weights_dir"]` 加载您随附的权重，将其放在 `meta["device"]` 上。返回一个暴露 `predict(X)` 的对象。
- `predict(X)` 接收已在 `meta["device"]` 上的 torch 批次 `X: (B, C, T)`；期望的输出形状取决于赛道（参见竞赛说明 — 例如类标签 `(B,)`、延迟 `(B,)`、嵌入 `(B, D)` 或关节角度序列 `(B, J, T)`）。

`meta` 还包含 `sfreq, ch_names, chs_info, n_chans, n_times` 和赛道的输出大小（`n_classes` / `n_outputs` / `n_joints`）。

可选地，实现 `fit(self, model, train_loader)` — 它仅在**本地**运行（从不在服务器上），让您通过起始工具包用确切的竞赛数据训练您的模型。

```python
import torch

import benchmark_utils  # noqa: F401 — 定位 compet_core
from compet_core.base_solver import CompetSolver


class Solver(CompetSolver):
    name = "MyModel"
    requirements = CompetSolver.requirements + ["pip::my-model-pkg"]

    def load_model(self, meta):
        model = build_my_model(
            n_chans=meta["n_chans"], n_times=meta["n_times"],
        )
        state = torch.load(meta["weights_dir"] / "weights.pt",
                           map_location=meta["device"])
        model.load_state_dict(state)
        return model.to(meta["device"]).eval()
```

您的 `predict` 可以是返回模型的一个方法（纯 PyTorch — 模型内不需要任何 benchopt、neuralset 或 neuralbench 知识）。

## 本地测试

起始工具包就是基准本身。从竞赛仓库运行（无需安装仓库 — `benchmark_utils` 定位共享的 `compet_core` 包）：

```bash
benchopt install tracks/<track>    # 求解器/数据集要求
benchopt run tracks/<track> -d Simulated   # 零下载烟雾测试
```

在上传前迭代提交，将您的 `submission.py` 放入赛道的 `solvers/` 文件夹并运行同一命令；或用摄取程序精确镜像平台：

```bash
python codabench/ingestion_program/ingestion.py \
    --submission-dir my_submission/ \
    --benchmark-dir tracks/<track> --datasets Simulated
python codabench/scoring_program/scoring.py \
    --prediction-dir output/ --output-dir scores/
```

本地在真实数据上训练：`python tools/setup_data.py --track <track>` 一次性下载，然后将您求解器的 `fit` 与 `benchopt run tracks/<track>` 一起使用。

## 提交

压缩提交文件夹（`submission.py` + 权重）并在*我的提交*选项卡上上传。基准和参考提交位于捆绑的 `solution/` 文件夹中。

pages.title: Timeline
pages.content:
# Timeline

## Warm-up phase — Sep 16 to Oct 15, 2026

Datasets, baselines and this starting kit are released; up to 5 submissions
per day. Use this phase to build and tune your model against the public
splits.

## Sealed final phase — Oct 16 to Nov 16, 2026 (AoE)

Up to 2 submissions per day; the final ranking is the best of your last five
sealed submissions, evaluated on held-out test data. The top-3 of each track
are re-run in a reproducibility audit.

## Winners announced — Dec 11–12, 2026

At the NeurIPS 2026 competition workshop in Sydney.
pages.content_zh:
# 时间表

## 热身阶段 — 2026年9月16日至10月15日

数据集、基线和启动工具包发布；每天最多可提交5次。在此阶段，使用公开数据集构建和调整你的模型。

## 密封最终阶段 — 2026年10月16日至11月16日（AoE）

每天最多可提交2次；最终排名基于你最后五次密封提交中的最佳成绩，在保留的测试数据上进行评估。每个赛道的前3名将进行可重复性审计。

## 获奖者公布 — 2026年12月11-12日

在悉尼举办的NeurIPS 2026竞赛工作坊上公布。
